overview: The Council met in executive session regarding ongoing litigation with BJ's Wholesale and approved several resolutions concerning municipal ordinances, funding requests, and contract legality. Significant discussions focused on police body camera contract terms and the potential regionalization of veteran services.

items.title: BJ's Wholesale Litigation
items.summary: The Council entered executive session to discuss legal strategy and receive an update on the pending litigation case of BJ's Wholesale Club versus Medford City Council.

items.title: National Grid Grant of Location
items.summary: Approved a grant of location for a new utility pole on Woodruff Avenue following a public hearing where councilors raised concerns about double poles and tree preservation.

items.title: Police Retirement and Meeting Records
items.summary: Congratulated Michael Goulding on his retirement as Chief of the Weston Police Department and approved the minutes of the previous meeting along with a committee report on intersection flooding.

items.title: Status of Draft Ordinances
items.summary: Approved a request for legal counsel to provide draft ordinances on nine items, including a $15 minimum wage for city employees, a polystyrene ban, and a housing stability task force.

items.title: CPA Funding Eligibility Requests
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that the School Department and Hormel Commission seek Community Preservation Act funding for locker room hot water repairs and athletic field maintenance.

items.title: Police Body Camera Contract Opinion
items.summary: Requested a legal opinion from the city solicitor on whether the 60-month police body camera contract complies with state laws that typically limit municipal contracts to 36 months.

items.title: Future Committee Meetings and COVID-19 Memorial
items.summary: Voted to schedule meetings to discuss 2022 council priorities and animal control staffing, and approved a resolution supporting the creation of a COVID-19 memorial grove.

items.title: Regionalization of Veteran Services
items.summary: Referred a proposal to merge veteran services with the Town of Winchester to the Subcommittee on Military and Veterans Affairs after councilors expressed differing views on regionalization.

items.title: Encore Entertainment Theater Expansion
items.summary: Approved a resolution thanking the community for its opposition to the Encore entertainment theater project after the developer withdrew its plans.
